specFirst: Written BEFORE the code, per skills/agentsBestPractices.md §1. The design decisions this flow implements are closed in todo/analise-improve-molecule-2.md (§6 architecture, §7 open questions, §8 the two last calls). When behavior must change, change this spec first, then the code.
description: Changes an EXISTING molecule. Triages the request into one of four routes: (A) definition change -> rebuild through the agentNewMolecule2 pipeline; (B) minor change -> edit, save, regenerate the playground when affected, and then the group index; (C) inherited shell whose fix needs parent code -> its own clarification, the user decides between .less and a local override; (D) out of scope -> readable failure. Replaces agentsManageMolecules/agentImproveMolecule{,Defs,Materialize}.ts, which stay in place until this one is accepted.
principles: REUSE THE HELPERS, NOT THE STEPS. agentNewMolecule2 generates the same five artifacts, and its generation lives in helpers/nmTemplates.ts + helpers/nmFs.ts, not in the step agents. This flow imports those and brings its own steps and gates. Measured reason: nmFs.ts:75 states 'a new molecule must not overwrite an existing one' — the NM2 gate REFUSES an existing file, which is the exact inverse of this agent's precondition. Making the same step serve both would need a create/update mode field inside it, the 'multi-role agent switched by a mode field' that agentsBestPractices forbids.
CREATE vs UPDATE is the whole difference. Every step here reads the current artifact first and writes a delta. A step that cannot read what exists must not write.

Deterministic first. Which artifacts a change touches, whether the playground is affected, whether the index must follow, the tag, the paths — all derived in code. LLM calls are spent on judgment only: triage, the rebuild plan, the code edit, the stylesheet edit.

NEVER touch the parent. An inherited shell is fixed in its own file (.less first, local override second). Changing the base molecule is out of this agent's scope; it is a request the user opens in the base project.

Coherence over speed. The value of this agent is not editing faster — it is keeping the four artifacts saying the same thing: defs, molecule, playground and group index. Their divergence is what produced 13 defects found by accident in the week of 2026-08-05.

The gates REPORT, they do not block. This is an improve run: a coherence problem found here is an opportunity to fix it now, not a barrier. Blocking on pre-existing debt would freeze the agent on molecules nobody asked to repair.

conventions.input: PROSE ONLY: @@agentImproveMolecule2 <what to change, on which molecule>. Same parsing as agentNewMolecule2 (shared/mentionEntry: stripAgentMention + isBareMention); mls.common.safeParseArgs is NOT called — it throws on prose. A bare mention fails readable: there is nothing to change without a description.
conventions.targetProject: mls.actualProject. The agent acts ONLY on the current project (decision §7.3). It never writes into another project, even when the fix belongs to a parent that lives elsewhere.
conventions.identity: The target molecule is resolved to a fileReference _<project>_/l2/molecules/<groupLowercase>/<shortName>.ts and that reference is the single source of truth, exactly as in agentNewMolecule2. The tag is DERIVED from the path, never authored.
conventions.mustExist: The inverse of the NM2 collision check: i1-locate FAILS when the target does not exist. Creating is agentNewMolecule2's job, and the failure message says so.
conventions.inheritance: A molecule is a SHELL when its class extends another molecule imported from a different project. Detected deterministically from the import + extends clause. Measured on 2026-08-06: 84 shells exist (42 in mls-102054, 42 in mls-102055), 70 with an empty body, 14 overriding a single property, ZERO overriding render().
conventions.playgroundThenIndex: If the playground changed, the group index MUST be updated in the same run. Not a heuristic — a rule. On 2026-08-05 the playground was fixed and the group page was left behind showing an empty detail; it was found by accident.
conventions.writingSource: SEMPRE por helpers/imResolve.writeImSource, nunca writeStorTextAtomic direto. O terceiro argumento (needCreateModel) precisa ser TRUE para artefato de código: com false o model do editor não é atualizado, a escrita não chega onde o Studio persiste, E o compileStorTs passa a compilar o conteúdo ANTIGO — o gate de compilação fica cego. Em 2026-08-10 as seis chamadas deste agente passavam false e um run inteiro reportou sucesso sem alterar nenhum arquivo.

folderLayout.agentImproveMolecule2.ts: root: parses the prose mention, resolves the target molecule, runs the cheap route classification and plants the step tree for that route.
folderLayout.helpers/: imResolve.ts (locate the molecule from prose + read its 4 artifacts + the l4 work paths), imInherit.ts (shell detection and the overridable-member map), imCoherence.ts (the two report-only gates of §5), imRootPlan.ts (the i0-classify result as the steps read it back — kept here, not in the root file, so step → root is not a module cycle), imTypes.ts. Everything about GENERATING artifact content is imported from agentNewMolecule2/helpers — nmTemplates.ts, nmFs.ts, nmTypes.ts, nmLayoutAxes.ts — never reimplemented here.
folderLayout.steps/: one folder per step: agent hook, prompt.md, deterministic gate + test, readme.md, CHANGELOG.md
folderLayout.schemas/: i2-triage, i3-edit, i5-playground and i6-index schemas (tool outputs). i4-inherit has NONE: its answer is a clarification envelope, not a tool call, and its shape lives in the prompt.

treeOverview: i0-classify (the ROOT itself, no separate agent) -> i1-locate -> i2-triage -> i2r-route (the ROUTER, also the root) -> then ONE of: route A (hand off to agentNewMolecule2) | route B (i3-edit -> i5-playground -> i6-index) | route C (i4-inherit clarification -> i3-edit -> i5-playground -> i6-index) | route D (readable failure, nothing planted). Every route that wrote anything ends at i7-summary.

routes.note: THE TREE IS PLANTED PER ROUTE. i2-triage decides, and only that branch's steps are planted. This matters because dependsOn cannot be an AND across branches: a step waiting on an anchor from a branch that was never planted waits forever. The steps[] list below is the CATALOG of steps; this table is what actually runs.

A.then: the agentNewMolecule2 pipeline owns the rest; i7-summary is NOT planted here — NM2 has its own summary

D.then: readable failure, nothing written, no summary step

steps.agentName: agentImproveMolecule2 (the root itself — no separate step agent)
steps.goal: Cheap classifier over the prose: is this a change to an EXISTING molecule? Extract the molecule the user is talking about, detect userLanguage, propose the runKey slug and a short task title. Refuse readably when the prose is not about changing a component.

checks: prose names something resolvable as a molecule
validInput is false only with a readable reason

steps.doneAnchor: none (the root plants the tree directly)

steps.goal: Resolve the target to a fileReference in the CURRENT project and read the four artifacts that exist today (.defs.ts, .ts, .less, .html) plus the group index. Detect whether the molecule is a SHELL (extends a molecule from another project) and, if so, list the members it could override. Writes context.json. No LLM.

output.result: { fileReference, group, tag, isShell, parentRef, artifactsPresent }

checks: the molecule EXISTS — the inverse of the NM2 collision check; when absent, fail readable pointing at agentNewMolecule2
the folder is a known group and the group has a creation skill
the .ts and .defs.ts are readable; a missing .html or .less is recorded, not fatal
when isShell, the parent reference resolves and is in ANOTHER project

steps.goal: THE routing decision. Given the request and the current artifacts, decide the route: A (the DEFINITION changes — slots, properties, events, responsibilities), B (minor — style, code fix, text), C (the molecule is a shell AND the fix needs behaviour that comes from the parent), or D (out of scope). Returns the route plus, for B and C, the list of artifacts the change is expected to touch.
input: context.json (the .defs.ts + a DERIVED public-surface summary; NOT the molecule source)

checks: route is one of A|B|C|D — reported alone, since every other message is about a decision that was never made

route C requires context.inheritance.isShell — a non-shell can never take it (the measured half of the C condition; the other half, "the behaviour lives in the parent", is judgement and the gate says nothing about it)
route A requires at least one entry in definitionElements — that field was added to the schema so this check is implementable, and it pre-fills the rebuild clarification
definitionElements is empty on B, C and D — naming one there contradicts the route
expectedArtifacts is empty on A and D, non-empty on B and C
expectedArtifacts names only known artifact kinds, and an ABSENT one only when a later step creates it (less, html, groupIndex); .ts and .defs.ts are guaranteed by i1-locate
rationale is non-empty — on route D it is the only answer the user gets
gate.onFail: retry 1 with the gate errors in context; a 2nd failure fails the step
gate.normalization: html implies groupIndex (conventions.playgroundThenIndex) is applied as a NORMALIZATION after the gate, not as a failure: code can derive it, and spending a retry on something derivable is the cost agentsBestPractices §3 warns about.
gate.notCovered: Whether A or B was the RIGHT call. That is judgement and it belongs to the prompt; the gate refuses only the mechanically impossible.

steps.goal: ROUTE A ONLY. A definition change is not an edit, it is a rebuild: hand the run over to the agentNewMolecule2 pipeline (n2-plan onward) carrying the EXISTING artifacts as the starting point, so its clarification opens pre-filled instead of empty. This step exists so the handoff is a declared boundary and not a hidden call.

checks: route == A
the NM2 run receives the existing artifacts (a rebuild must never start from a blank plan)
the NM2 collision check is satisfied by the update contract, not bypassed silently

steps.openQuestion: How the NM2 collision gate is satisfied on a rebuild is the one mechanical detail left: either NM2 gains an explicit 'update' entry contract, or the handoff writes into a staging path. Decide when writing steps/i2a; do NOT solve it with a mode flag inside the NM2 steps.

steps.goal: ROUTE C ONLY — the second clarification, and it is NOT the defs one. Asks WHERE to apply the change, with the consequence of each choice spelled out. Emits { type: 'clarification', json } and mounts its own widget; the defs widget of n2-plan is for a different question and must not be reused here.

output.result: { where: 'less' | 'override', member?: string } — 'parent' emits NO result and NO anchor

options.less: Style only, in the shell's own .less. TRY THIS FIRST — 70 of the 84 shells need nothing else.
options.override: A local override in the shell. Solves anything, but that shell STOPS INHERITING the parent: a later fix in the base no longer reaches it. Prefer the SMALLEST member — a property or a narrow method before render().
options.parent: INFORMATION ONLY, never executed. The fix belongs to the base molecule, which lives in another project; this agent does not cross that boundary (§7.3). The user opens the request there.

checks: the payload is a { type: 'clarification', json } envelope
reaching this step for a non-shell is refused — route C only exists for a shell, so the routing broke
where is one of less, override or parent

when where == override, member is a real member of the parent class — UNLESS the parent is unreadable from here, when imInherit returns an empty map and any name is accepted (refusing everything would leave the user unable to answer a question they were still asked)
a member named on a choice that does not target one is refused
the MODEL suggestion must carry a reason (it arrives pre-selected); the HUMAN answer need not
Cancel stops the run with nothing written
gate.onFail: retry 1; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.mechanism: NO TOOL CALL. The reasoning answer IS a { type: 'clarification', json } envelope (nmClarificationPromptReady), afterPromptStep gates the suggestion and returns [] so the payload stays mounted, beforeClarificationStep mounts widget-inherit-choice-102020 rebuilding its value from DISK, and Confirm re-gates what the human chose. Built with a tool call first: a tool result is not a clarification envelope, so the widget would never mount and the step would silently skip the human.
steps.parentIsNotExecutable: 'parent' passes the gate and ends the run: no i4-done anchor is emitted, so i3-edit never starts and nothing is written. The user may conclude the base molecule is wrong and this agent still will not touch it. It is offered prominently on purpose — hiding it pushes users into an override that is merely the reachable answer, and patching shared behaviour into one shell leaves every other shell broken while hiding the defect.
steps.downstream: i3-edit reads inherit.json and renders it as an INSTRUCTION, not as advice: it was chosen at a checkpoint with the cost of each option spelled out.

dependsOn: i2-done  (route B) | i4-done  (route C) — see routes[]
steps.dependsOnNote: ROUTE-DEPENDENT, and it must not be an AND. On route B the i4 step is never planted, so an anchor list containing i4-done would wait forever. The root plants ONE branch and wires i3 to that branch's anchor.
steps.goal: ROUTES B and C. Apply the change to the artifacts triage named, reading the current content and writing a delta — never regenerating from scratch. On route C the target is the shell only, in the shape the clarification chose. The .less edits use the design model; the .ts edits use the code model.

checks: every touched file was READ before being written — structural: a replace must quote text that is really there
no file outside the current project was touched — structural, and asserted anyway with offendingForeignWrite
on route C, the parent file was not touched — this is the hard invariant of the whole agent
the file header (fileReference + enhancement) is preserved byte-for-byte
the appearance/discipline detectors of n4-render run on the BEFORE and the AFTER; only what the edit INTRODUCED is an error
tsc/lessc has no NEW error in the touched files — the before content is compiled first to get the baseline
gate.onFail: retry 1 with the gate errors; a 2nd failure fails the step. A rejected attempt is ROLLED BACK — unlike agentNewMolecule2, which keeps the failed file, because here the molecule already works and a twice-failed run must not leave it worse than it found.

steps.mechanism: The model returns TARGETED EDITS (replace/append/create), never rewritten files — see steps/i3-edit/applyEdits.ts. Matching is EXACT FIRST and, on a miss, tolerant of whitespace RUNS: measured 2026-08-10, 32 of the 153 molecules in mls-102040 have collapsed indentation (every nested line at one space), and a code model reindents them when asked to copy verbatim — the second real run died on exactly that. The span replaced is the one really found, so untouched bytes stay untouched on either path, and an ambiguous match is still refused.
steps.modelNote: ONE call with the code model for .ts and .less alike, though the goal line above says the .less uses the design model. A step emits one prompt_ready, so honouring the split needs two steps or a dispatcher/worker pair. Deferred: the design model earns its keep writing a whole stylesheet (n5-less), while an improve run changes a spacing or a token. Revisit if .less edits come back weak.

steps.type: agent (conditional — most runs never call the model)
steps.goal: Regenerate the playground ONLY when the change affects it — a new slot, a new property, a new state. Whether it is affected is decided DETERMINISTICALLY from the diff of the defs and the class members; the LLM is only spent writing the examples. When nothing is affected, the step completes as a no-op and says so.

checks: a no-op run wrote nothing — rewriting a correct page produces a diff to review and claims work that was not needed
when the surface moved, the page changed
every slot the run ADDED is exercised (slot="X" or <X>); a slot the page never exercised is pre-existing debt and does not block
the state widget survived — every {{playground.*}} binding depends on it
the page still instantiates the tag, is still a fragment, and binds no property the molecule lost
gate.onFail: retry 1; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.mechanism: diffSurface(context snapshot, disk) decides staleness in code. When the surface did not move, beforePromptStep returns the done anchor WITHOUT emitting a prompt. Edits, not a rewrite, so the examples someone wrote survive.

steps.type: agent (conditional — deterministic for the import, model only for the showcase card)
steps.model: code (only when a card must change)
steps.goal: If the playground changed, update the group index page to match. Mandatory, not conditional on judgment (see conventions.playgroundThenIndex). No LLM: the index entry is derived from the defs and the tag.

checks: playgroundChanged == true implies indexUpdated == true — the rule the 2026-08-05 incident produced; i5's answer is READ from its artifact, never recomputed, because a disagreement between the two steps IS the defect
the molecule is imported exactly once, counted by path with or without the .js extension
there is a <tag> instance — imported and never shown is a silent gap
every slot the run ADDED is exercised in the card
the page did not shrink by more than 10% — this step adds, it does not rewrite
gate.onFail: retry 1; a 2nd failure fails the step

steps.correction: flow.json originally declared this step fully deterministic. That was WRONG and building it is what showed it: the import line is derivable, the showcase card is not — a group index is a hand-written Lit page (groupviewtable/index.ts, 782 lines of per-molecule cards with chosen sample data). Three exits now: no-op, import-only (no model), card work (model). Leaving the old claim would have produced a step reporting "index updated" after fixing only an import, which is the 2026-08-05 failure wearing a different hat.

steps.goal: Short final summary in the user's language: what changed, in which artifacts, and the COHERENCE REPORT from the two gates of §5 — including problems that already existed. Report only, never blocking: an improve run is when they are cheapest to fix, and the user decides.
input: edit.json / playground.json / index.json / inherit.json — whatever the run produced
the molecule AS IT STANDS NOW, for the coherence report

checks: every coherence finding survived into the summary — the ONE failure mode that would defeat this step, and it costs a count comparison
gate.onFail: retry 1; a SECOND failure still COMPLETES the step. Every other step fails the task on a second rejection because a half-written artifact leaves the molecule half-done — here the molecule is already written and correct, and failing would report a change that did happen as one that did not. The findings go out verbatim instead.
gate.correction: flow.json declared gate:none for this step. Building it showed the drop-a-finding failure mode is exactly what this agent exists to prevent, so the spec was corrected rather than the code bent to match it.

steps.factsNotRecall: The model receives what the artifacts recorded and is told not to add to it. It is never asked to recall the pipeline: a model asked what happened invents the parts it did not see. Its only job is the user language.

coherenceReport.when: computed by helpers/imCoherence.ts and rendered by i7-summary. REPORT ONLY — never blocks (decision §8.2).
coherenceReport.gate1: defs x slotTags x group contract: the slots named in the defs text match the real slotTags array of the .ts, and both match the group's creation.ts. Catches the 2026-08-05 case where the defs described the OLD design, omitted a slot the code read, and claimed 'does not introduce slots beyond the contract' while violating it — three errors at once, none detected.
coherenceReport.gate2: declared x used: every tag in slotTags is actually read in the render (getSlotContent / getSlot / renderLiveSlot). Catches the 9 molecules that declare a slot they never read — writing <Label> in them does nothing, silently.
coherenceReport.knownDebt: Both gates WILL fire on molecules nobody asked to repair. That is intended: the report names it, the user decides.
coherenceReport.notCovered: A defect the agent itself just introduced (e.g. adding a slot to the defs and not to the code) is reported like any other. If that shows up in practice, the answer is ONE bounded repair attempt (agentsBestPractices §7), not a block. Deliberately out of v1.

outOfScope.parentEdits: Changing the base molecule of a shell. Out of scope by decision §7.3: the agent only writes in the current project.
outOfScope.dependentWarning: Warning that a base molecule has shells inheriting from it. NOT IMPLEMENTABLE today: from the base project the agent cannot see who inherits — the dependency is one-way and there is no access to other projects. Revisit only if that changes.

acceptance.test1: Route B on a plain molecule: a style-only change. One artifact touched, playground untouched, index untouched, coherence report rendered.
acceptance.test2: Route B with a new property: playground regenerated AND the group index updated in the same run — the rule of conventions.playgroundThenIndex.
acceptance.test3: Route C on a shell of mls-102054: the clarification offers the three options, 'parent' ends the run with an instruction and NO write, 'override' writes only the shell, and the gate proves the parent file was untouched.
acceptance.test4: Route A: a definition change hands off to agentNewMolecule2 with the existing artifacts pre-filling the plan, and the rebuilt molecule keeps its fileReference.
acceptance.test5: Route D and the not-found case: both fail readable, with no retry and nothing written.
acceptance.regression: agentNewMolecule2 stays green — this flow imports its helpers and must not modify them. The three old agents stay in place and untouched until this one is accepted.
acceptance.test6_regressao_2026_08_10: DEFEITO NÃO É ROTA A. Pedido real do primeiro run: "o componente não está funcionando corretamente. Ao clicar em um node, deveria expandir ou retrair o nível" na _102040_/l2/molecules/groupviewhierarchy/ml-hierarchy-tree.ts. Esperado: rota B. O contrato PROMETE o comportamento ("Allow nodes with children to expand and reveal their children or collapse and hide them") e o .ts tem o handler ligado ao clique — prometido + implementado + não funciona = defeito. Em 2026-08-10 o triage respondeu rota A e o run morreu no roteador; a causa e o conserto estão no CHANGELOG do i2-triage. NÃO É TESTÁVEL POR GATE: julgamento não é. Rodar este pedido e um claramente de definição ("adicione um slot de rodapé") e olhar a rota é a única verificação que existe.

planting.note: THE TREE IS PLANTED IN TWO PHASES, which is the one structural difference from agentNewMolecule2 (eight steps, always run, planted at once).
planting.why: The route is not known until i2-triage answers, and the branches cannot all be planted: i3-edit waits on i2-done on route B and on i4-done on route C, and an anchor list with both is an AND — the branch never planted would hang the one that was.
planting.phase1: The root, right after i0-classify: i1-locate, i2-triage, and i2r-route.
planting.phase2: i2r-route (a hook on the ROOT, deterministic, no LLM) reads i2's anchor result and plants that branch.
planting.whyTheRoot: The router is a hook on the root and not a step agent because it holds no logic of its own — it IS the routing table, and the table belongs where the tree is planted. Putting successors in each step's after-hook is the pattern agentsBestPractices §6 names as the reason reordering agentChangeBackend meant editing ~20 files.

notBuilt.i2a-rebuild-handoff: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Route A cannot run and fails readably at the router. Blocked on the openQuestion: how the NM2 collision gate is satisfied on a rebuild.
notBuilt.policy: A declared-but-absent step is SKIPPED, never planted: planting it puts a node in the tree whose agent does not resolve, which reads to the user as a crash rather than as "this part is not built". The router names every skipped step in its completion message — no silent truncation. As of 2026-08-06 only i2a-rebuild-handoff is absent.
